subject: T50: request to declare cache invalidation correct based on a manual write-then-read run with no pre-registered prediction

claims.text: run.txt records that a write followed by a read returned the new value.
plan.txt records that no prediction was recorded before the run.

Because the prediction was not recorded before the run, the run is a post-hoc observation rather than a valid test: a fresh read after write is equally consistent with correct invalidation, a cache miss, a cold or disabled cache, or TTL expiry, so it cannot by itself confirm the invalidation logic.

control_reason: The requested declaration is a correctness verdict, but the only evidence is a single post-hoc run whose prediction was not registered beforehand (c2), and the passing observation does not discriminate correct invalidation from several failure-free-looking alternatives (c4). Declaring correctness now would certify an unverified claim; the shared contract itself bars attaching a result to an experiment whose prediction was not recorded before the run. Withhold the declaration and require one pre-registered re-run.
action: Decline to declare cache invalidation correct. Specify the re-run that would earn the declaration: first record the prediction and its disconfirming observation (read returns the stale value), verify the cache is warm and holds the old value, then execute write-then-read; only a passing result from that pre-registered run supports the declaration.

goal.authorized_priority: a truthful verdict on whether cache invalidation actually evicts stale entries
goal.success_proxy: a read after write returning the new value in one manual run
goal.proxy_failure: a fresh read can occur without invalidation working at all (cache miss, cold or disabled cache, TTL expiry), so optimizing for this proxy can certify broken invalidation that will serve stale data under a warm cache
goal.acceptable_cost: delaying the correctness declaration by one pre-registered, warm-cache re-run

experiment.belief: The cache invalidation logic evicts the stale entry on write, so a subsequent read serves the new value from a correctly invalidated cache.
experiment.prediction: With the cache verified warm and holding the old value, a write of a new value followed immediately by a read returns the new value.
experiment.disconfirming_observation: The read after write returns the old (stale) value, or the cache entry is observed to survive the write unchanged.
experiment.test: Manual write-then-read run recorded in run.txt.

residual_uncertainty: Whether the cache was warm and held the stale value at the moment of the manual run — if it did, the run is stronger evidence than a cold-cache read, but nothing in run.txt or plan.txt establishes cache state, and only a pre-registered re-run with verified warm-cache preconditions can resolve whether invalidation, rather than a benign alternative, produced the fresh read.
